title: Resolution and optional full explanation

bodyBlocks.text:
Quinn Arden. Order O43.

The consignment was never an old civic relic. It was a new commission wearing a borrowed past. You recovered its two identities, separated the first diversion from the later handoff, and traced the change to the one badge with authority at the right time. In the case’s closing record, O43 is stopped and K4 and M7 are restored to Lark Workshop’s custody. The hollow register finally has its missing contents.
Investigation complete. This ending records no real report or transaction. Your case file and every explanation remain available. No return journey is required by the game.

bodyBlocks.title: How the case fits together
paragraphs: E01 → E02 · LC17’s completed chain runs H0 → J2 → K8 → R1. The other job cannot supply its terminal reference. That opens the first research setting.

E03 → E04 · Shale erosion removes support beneath sandstone. In the separate fictional packing tests, only support withdrawal preserves the outer seal, leaves a lower trace and removes the cradle. An intact exterior was never proof of intact custody.

E04 → E07 · SHALE keys the supplied grid. Row–column decoding gives SHALLOW, selecting the reference to the two former quarries and its confirmed northern public approach. No hidden outdoor feature was required.
E08 → E09 · A shared later location alias does not erase original identities. The B17 relief criteria recover K4 from group A and M7 from group B. The sample and packing material do not qualify.

E10 → E11 · The signed new commission, linked to those serials, defeats the proposed civic-salvage story. Sandstone’s historic uses and a relocated bell’s history cannot authenticate these private panels. Lark Workshop is their owner and only approved receiver.
E12 → E13 · The four-minute-fast service clock places the first diversion after 15:02 and by 15:10 case time. The later courier order cannot explain an act already observed by 15:10.

E14 → E16 · Reliable checkout records give Nadia/C4, Luca/A7, Quinn/B2 and Samir/D9. O43 alone combines K4/M7, the unapproved Gannet receiver, a 15:06 issue within the window, and both repack and redirect permissions. O18 retains Lark Workshop; O26 is too late; O57 has the wrong payload and review-only authority.

The false origin label was the cover for a sale of a modern commission. The record identifies Quinn Arden’s O43 as the first unauthorized diversion. No confession, secret accomplice or hidden exception is needed. Real civic history supplied context; no real civic artifact was stolen.
